title: Workaholic: why AI makes you work more, and 5 rules against performative productivity
summary: Ruben argues AI removes the friction of both starting and stopping, so people ship more but move in the wrong direction. He names the enemy "performative productivity" and gives 5 rules plus two prompts to pick one goal and audit your week against it. He backs it with an 8-month Harvard study showing AI intensifies work.

principles.text: AI removes the friction of starting and stopping, so busyness feels like progress.
principles.quote: AI removes the friction of _starting_. That’s great. But it also removes the friction of _stopping_. And if stopping feels harder than continuing, you have an addiction.

principles.text: The hardest part of work is deciding what's worth doing; AI lets you skip it, producing circular momentum.
principles.quote: AI lets you skip the hardest part of work: deciding what’s _worth_ doing in the first place.

principles.text: Before prompting, state the problem in one sentence; otherwise AI generates noise you then edit all night.
principles.quote: If you can’t explain the problem in one sentence, AI will generate noise. And you’ll spend your night editing that noise.

principles.text: Subtract as deliberately as you add: kill 3 tasks for every 1 task AI helps you add.
principles.quote: For every new thing AI helps you ship, ask: what 3 things can I stop doing?

principles.text: Set a hard 'last prompt' time; rest is the most productive behavior.
principles.quote: Understand that the most productive behavior you can have is to rest.

principles.text: AI writes v1, but you decide whether v1 should exist; fast drafting is not a reason to draft.
principles.quote: Just because AI can draft something in 30 seconds doesn’t mean it should be drafted.
